name: Marie Curie
branch: While examining pitchblende, Curie found radioactivity stronger than uranium alone could explain.
discovery: Discovery of polonium and radium; foundational work on radioactivity.
struggle: Gender barriers, limited laboratory conditions, radiation danger and institutional scepticism.
impact: Radioactivity reshaped physics, chemistry, medicine and cancer treatment.
keywords: radioactivity polonium radium pitchblende chemistry physics cancer radiation

name: Rosalind Franklin
branch: X-ray diffraction images captured crucial structural evidence about DNA.
discovery: Photo 51 and related DNA analysis helped reveal the double-helix structure.
struggle: Under-recognition, contested credit and a difficult institutional environment.
impact: Her evidence became part of the foundation of modern genetics and molecular biology.
keywords: dna x-ray diffraction photo 51 double helix genetics molecular biology

name: Katherine Johnson
branch: Hand-calculated trajectories for America’s early human spaceflights.
discovery: Trajectory calculations for Alan Shepard, John Glenn and Apollo-era missions.
struggle: Worked through racial segregation, sexism and the invisibility of “human computers”.
impact: Her calculations helped make crewed American spaceflight safer and more precise.
keywords: nasa orbit trajectory alan shepard john glenn apollo mathematics space human computer

name: Tu Youyou
branch: Studied traditional medical texts and tested sweet wormwood extracts scientifically.
struggle: Worked under intense public-health pressure with delayed international recognition.
impact: Artemisinin therapies improved and saved millions of lives worldwide.
keywords: malaria artemisinin sweet wormwood medicine public health parasites

name: Katalin Karikó
branch: Found that modified RNA building blocks could reduce unwanted inflammatory reactions.
discovery: Nucleoside base modifications that helped enable effective mRNA vaccines.
struggle: Years of scepticism, funding difficulty and career setbacks before recognition.
impact: Her work helped make rapid mRNA vaccine development possible.
keywords: mrna vaccine covid nucleoside base modifications biochemistry immunology rna

name: Donna Strickland
branch: Created a way to amplify ultrashort laser pulses without destroying the amplifier.
discovery: Chirped pulse amplification for high-intensity lasers.
struggle: Long-delayed recognition in a field where women were historically underrepresented.
impact: CPA became essential for high-intensity lasers, including uses in eye surgery.
keywords: laser chirped pulse amplification cpa physics optics eye surgery

name: Chien-Shiung Wu
branch: Designed the cobalt-60 experiment that tested whether parity is conserved in beta decay.
discovery: Experimental proof that parity is not conserved in weak interactions.
struggle: Faced sexism, racism and Nobel-era under-recognition despite decisive experimental work.
impact: The Wu experiment reshaped particle physics and our understanding of symmetry.
keywords: parity beta decay cobalt nuclear physics weak interaction symmetry wu experiment

name: Jocelyn Bell Burnell
branch: Spotted a repeating radio signal while analysing telescope chart recordings as a graduate student.
discovery: Discovery of pulsars: rapidly rotating neutron stars emitting regular radio pulses.
struggle: Her role was widely discussed after the Nobel Prize went to senior male colleagues.
impact: Pulsars became powerful tools for astrophysics, gravity research and cosmic timing.
keywords: pulsars radio astronomy astrophysics neutron stars cambridge telescope
